Epitaph

EP-ih-taf · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Epitaph is words inscribed on a tombstone or monument in memory of the person buried there.

The old headstone's epitaph, worn nearly smooth by two centuries of rain, simply read, "Beloved by all who knew her."

Worked Example

For his epitaph, the retired sea captain had chosen a single line from his favorite sailing poem, carved beneath his name and the years of his life.

An epitaph is the short written inscription itself -- the words carved in stone -- rather than the ceremony or a poem read aloud at a funeral.

How Epitaph Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

inscription

inscription: words carved, written, or engraved onto a surface, especially as a memorial

memorial

memorial: something built or done to honor the memory of a person or event

Antonyms

birth announcement

birth announcement: a notice celebrating the arrival of a new baby

christening

christening: a ceremony marking a baby's naming and welcome

How Strong Is It? — label → epitaph → monument

label vs. epitaph

label vs. epitaph: A label is just a short piece of identifying text, with no special weight or sentiment.

monument vs. epitaph

monument vs. epitaph: A whole monument is built and dedicated to a memory, far more elaborate than a single carved epitaph.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — epi-

prefix — epi-: upon, above (Greek)

root — taphos

root — taphos: tomb (Greek)

Put it together

Put it together: Epitaph comes from Greek epi- ("upon") + taphos ("tomb") -- literally "upon the tomb," the words placed on a grave marker.

Use the root in a new word: epicenter

Use the root in a new word: epicenter: Scientists rushed to the epicenter of the earthquake to measure how the ground had shifted.
